workflows.name: High-pressure dispersion of chemically isolated cellulose nanocrystals
workflows.title: Kröger et al. 2023, phosphorylated CNC isolation
workflows.locator: Experimental Section: Washing and Dispersion of Nanocrystals, printed p. 1320.
workflows.scope: The source disperses chemically modified and hydrolyzed CNC feed using M-110P. This plan begins with washed, already chemically isolated CNCs. It does not replace hydrolysis or describe purely mechanical CNF production. Alternative models need sample compatibility, chamber and process qualification.
workflows.output: Aqueous CNC dispersion with coarse aggregates removed
workflows.units: Feed concentration wt%, process pressure bar, passes count and chamber/filter size µm in the cited example. Exact settings remain scoped to that phosphorylated-CNC study.
steps: Record chemical pretreatment, solids concentration and feed volume. The source example uses already modified/hydrolyzed, washed feed.
Disperse the CNC feed at high pressure
Choose sample-compatible interaction chamber, cooling and pressure/pass settings. The source M110P example is not a universal setting for all models.
Screen coarse aggregates with the reported mesh
Manual consumable operation. The source reports a 10 µm mesh filter. This is not an automated ultrafiltration-machine requirement. Record retained/discarded fractions and recovery.
Check crystal morphology and retained crystallinity
Use diffraction with microscopy to assess the product. Do not treat hydrodynamic size as proof of individual crystal dimensions.

workflows.title: Peng et al. 2012, spray drying CNC and NFC suspensions

Nanoscale individual crystals, unchanged morphology and reversible redispersion are not guaranteed. Alternative dryers require feed, solvent, containment and operating qualification.
workflows.output: Dry CNC-containing powder or agglomerates for recovery assessment
workflows.units: CNC feed wt%, inlet temperature °C, liquid feed mL/min and atomizing-gas flow L/h are reported in the cited parameter study. Water evaporation kg/h or mL/h is an equipment specification, not dry-CNC yield.
steps: Prepare and homogenize the aqueous CNC feed
Record solids loading and feed history. Keep CNC and CNF/NFC sample identities separate.
Atomize and dry the qualified feed
Record dryer configuration, feed rate, inlet/outlet conditions and atomization gas. Use a reviewed material-specific protocol.
Contain the powder, weigh the collected fraction and document wall/filter losses. The cyclone and collection hardware are part of the selected dryer configuration.
Review powder morphology and a documented rewetting trial before claiming individual nanocrystals or ready redispersion.

workflows.output: Aqueous CNC/aggregate dispersion with documented redispersion assessment
workflows.units: Record solids concentration, mixing or ultrasound time and energy/temperature as appropriate for the chosen protocol. No numeric operating settings were verified from the source abstract.
steps: Wet the characterized dry CNC powder
Record powder identity, drying history, solids loading and the liquid phase.
Apply the selected stirred or ultrasonic dispersion method
These are alternative treatment branches. Select the intended protocol and record conditions; no arbitrary sonication setting is supplied.
Record the assessed morphology and any remaining aggregates. Failure to redisperse is a valid recorded result.
Measure dispersion behavior and archive recovery data
DLS is a supplementary dispersion/aggregate indicator, not a direct CNC length measurement. Record sample preparation and use microscopy to interpret anisotropic rods.

io_records.units_of_measure: mL. psi.

io_records.inputs_and_states: Liquid emulsion or solids-in-liquid suspension; adjustable process pressure. Electric/hydraulic drive 1.5 kW; listed power 230 V, 60 Hz. Product page states no compressed air or hydraulic cooling water is needed.
io_records.outputs_and_states: Processed liquid suspension/emulsion. Exact CNC dispersion use is demonstrated in Kröger et al. 2023; see workflow notes. Actual particle dimensions and recovery are measured results, not fixed equipment outputs.
io_records.units_of_measure: mL/min. mL. psi. bar. kW. V. Hz.

primary_cnc_reference_notes.title: Efficient Isolation Method for Highly Charged Phosphorylated Cellulose Nanocrystals
primary_cnc_reference_notes.exact_methods_locator: Experimental Section, printed p. 1320 (PDF page 4 including Aalto cover), consecutive subsections HCl Gas Hydrolysis of Modified Fibers, Washing, and Dispersion of Nanocrystals.
primary_cnc_reference_notes.supported_claim: After phosphorylation, gaseous-HCl hydrolysis and washing, the authors disperse the produced CNCs using Microfluidics M-110P. Washed material in water at 1 wt% passes three times at 1500 bar through paired Z-type 400 and 200 µm collision chambers, followed by 10 µm mesh filtration.
primary_cnc_reference_notes.equipment_match: M110P is an exact named-model match. It supports CNC dispersion after chemical treatment, not stand-alone CNF-to-CNC conversion by mechanical homogenization.
primary_cnc_reference_notes.input_state: Hydrolyzed, washed phosphorylated cellulose suspended in water.
primary_cnc_reference_notes.output_state: Aqueous phosphorylated CNC dispersion; large aggregates are excluded by a following filtration step.
primary_cnc_reference_notes.claim_limits: The conditions and measured results belong to this phosphorylated-CNC experiment. Do not present them as universal settings, a recipe for other CNCs, or all-model capabilities.

primary_cnc_reference_notes.equipment_match: B-290 is an exact named-model match for drying CNC suspension. The title uses broad historical terminology; the methods explicitly distinguish the CNC and NFC sample streams.
primary_cnc_reference_notes.input_state: Aqueous CNC suspension, diluted from the supplied 6.5 wt% suspension.
primary_cnc_reference_notes.output_state: Dry CNC-derived particles with spherical/donut-like morphologies; this is not proof of individually separated CNCs or spontaneous redispersion.
primary_cnc_reference_notes.claim_limits: No DOI verified. Public author PDF uses pp. 1–14, so final publisher pagination is deliberately left null. The study's parameter values are examples, not equipment performance guarantees.

primary_cnc_reference_notes.title: Aggregate Morphology and Aqueous Dispersibility of Spray-Dried Powders of Cellulose Nanocrystals
primary_cnc_reference_notes.verified_locator: Publisher Abstract. Full methods were not accessible in the bounded search; do not invent a dryer model or methods subsection.
primary_cnc_reference_notes.supported_claim: Spray drying acid-hydrolyzed CNC suspensions forms granular aggregates that are difficult to redisperse to individual particles. The study investigates cospray drying with a nonionic surfactant and compares static, stirred and ultrasound-assisted aqueous dispersion.
primary_cnc_reference_notes.equipment_match: Category-level drying/aggregation evidence only; no exact dryer-model claim verified.
primary_cnc_reference_notes.claim_limits: Use for the aggregation/redispersion caveat. Use Peng et al. 2012 for accessible exact B-290 methods evidence.
